newsitem.title: BULGARIA: France extradites suspected Bulgarian embezzler.
newsitem.headline: France extradites suspected Bulgarian embezzler.

text.p: Ivo Nedialkov, whose pyramid investment scheme wiped out the savings of thousands of Bulgarians, was extradited from France on Tuesday.

"Now that he is here, Ivo Nedialkov will be placed under investigation and if found guilty of embezzling large sums of money, faces up to 19 years in prison," a prosecutor's office spokeswoman told Reuters.
French police detained Nedialkov, 31, in the Riviera resort of Cannes last August.

His East West International Holding Group collapsed in 1994, costing 9,000 Bulgarians their savings. Investigators estimate that he misappropriated around 360 million levs -- $10 million at the exchange rates of the time -- by using income from new investors to pay off old investors at ever-rising prices.
Unsound investment schemes swept many East European countries in which the collapse of communism left a public at the mercy of deceit in a capitalist economy few of them understood.

Some 30,000 Bulgarians lost an estimated $25 million to promoters who fled abroad. Michael Kapustin, accused of misappropriation of more than $10 million, was extradited from Germany last year and awaits trial.
The most extreme case was long-isolated Albania where the frauds led to a major social and political upheaval this year.
